KANAWANA — 


RAPPORT ANNUEL DU DIRECTEUR 
DIRECTOR'S ANNUAL REPORT 


KAMP KANAWANA 1978 


DIRECTOR'S REPORT 


aeeeeel am happy to send my greetings to all Kampers and staff of 
Kamp Kanawana. 


Kamp Kanawana provides an opportunity for many young people across 
Canada to learn about each other's culture in a natural and healthy 
environment. 


La dimension Internationale qul s'est ajoutée cette année rehaussera 
sGrement l'esprit d'entraide et de coopération afin de cultiver une 
jeunesse saine et vigoureuse. 


Dans cet esprit, je suis heureux de vous souhalter de bonnes 
vacances. Mes mellleurs voeux & tous pout une celebration reussie. 


Pierre Elliott Trudeau 


Prime Minister - Premler Ministre 


The 85th season of Kamp Kanawana has come to an end. It was a summer 
filled with many wonderful highlights along with some disappointments 
and difficulties. It is my Intention to point out some of these with 
a view to assist in the preparation of Kamp Kanawana '79 as well as 
providing some insight to the staff of '78. 


KAMPERS : 


Our registration for 1978 Increased by 9% over 1977 and slightly 
surpassed the budgeted number of camper weeks (1200). We had 442 
different children making up the 1227 camper weeks. 


Other Significant Notes: 


- French population was 27% 

- 60% of 1977 kampers returned in 1978 

- Slightly over 33% of the kampers were from single parent homes 

~ Almost 5% of our kamper population was from the Laurentian area 
(St. Jovite, Ste Adele, St. Sauveur, St. Jerome, etc.) 

- Kampers came to Kamp Kanawana from Montreal, Ottawa, Toronto, 
Chateauguay, Quebec City, Three Rivers, Hudson, Poland, New York, 
Charlottetown, New Jersey, Virginia, North Carolina, Saskatoon, 
Otterburn, West Island, the Laurentians, St. Hubert, St. Lazare, 
St. Foy, Franklin Centre, Trinidad, Valleyfield and Indiana.

In terms of discipline, 7 kampers were sent home during the summer. 
Four of these were because of drugs, two for cigarette and one due to 
an injury. 


STAFF: 


— 


Unfortunately, | cannot say the same this year as | did last, 
regarding the staff. Most of the staff did an excellent job with our 
kampers. | was particularly impressed with a number of our new 
counsellors who very auickly adapted to a new work situation in a 
very effective way. 


At the same time, | did have difficulties with some of the staff. 

1, the Assistant Camp Director, Kerry Finucan and other senior staff 
became very frustrated and disappointed with the attitudes and 
behaviour of some of our staff. At the half-way point of the summer, 
| spoke to the entire staff about my concerns, the kamp policies and 
objectives, etc. In some respects, this normalized the situation. 
However, for certain individuals what was said was to no avail. | 
believe at this stage it will be necessary to not accept a great 
number of the staff wishing to return. 


| hope that the staff who will not be rehired will understand the 
reasons and hopefully mature as a result. 

To the staff who ‘kept their heads above it all' and affected 
children in a positive way, | extend my sincerest thanks. 


To my assistant Kerry Finucan, a special thanks for his constant 
support and help throughout the summer.

STAFF TRAINING: 


The staff training started in February of this year with participation 
at conferences and meetings. The 8 day pre-kamp program was good. 
Kerry Finucan and other staff spent much time in preparing various 
sessions. It was well worth the effort. The following should be 
considered in this program for 1979: 


- More emphasis on canoeing and camping skills. 

Repeat the film ‘Cipher in the Snow’ and discussion 
about ‘making a kid feel like a somebody’. 

Retatn sessions on teaching and program resourcefulness. 
Retain session with naturalists from Mont St. Hilaire. 
Clarify policies and attitudes to staff (here and in 
staff manual). 

Send someone to an Astronomy Instructor's School. 
Initiate a formal ongoing training for staff during 

the summer. 

Plan to have a rainy day or 
when it rains. (6 out of 9 


two that can be fitted In 


days In '78)

Ontario Camping Association - Conference: 4 people

Some staff have intimated that they feel the strictness of the 
Director Inhibits the kamp spirit. This attitude should be dispelled 
in pre~kamp and better explained to potential staff during interviews.

Program Continued 
Some specific recommendations for '79 programs are: 


~ Interest groups should be re-thought out. 

(see Assistant Camp Director's report for details) 

- Re-look at program supplies with a view to increasing 
them, especially the small items. 

- Continue with only one swimming area, but enlarge it 
by 50% in order to accommodate more people. Consider 
locating it by the junior parking lot. 

- Improve system of equipment control ~ a number of things 
were ‘lost’. 

~ 8 canoes have been sent out to be re~canvassed. At 
least another 8 or 10 should be sent. 

~ Purchase 4 non-wood rowboats. 

~ Have new centre boards and rudders made for the Arrow 
sailboats. 

- Continue the work on the Hebertism course. 

- Study present cord system for swimming. 

- Some attention is required to protect the paddles. 
More are required and those that are there need some 
sort of fibreglass band to protect them. 

- Consider adding a couple of new major programs eg 
riding, tenis, kayaking, photography, etc.

HEALTH & SAFETY: 
Again this summer, we were fortunate to have had a Kamp Doctor. 
Doctors Sharon Levine and Suzanne Tha were always avallable to holp 
augment the excellent care aiven by Nurses Gisela Roch and Therese 
Marin with Assistant Nurse Rachel Michie. 


Generally speaking, health at kamp was very good. The weather and 
kitchen did help this a great deal. 


There was the odd emergency trip required. There were 3 fractures and 
one appendectomy. Also, a few kampers had head IIce. This was 
cloared up quickly by a thorough cleaning of all the cabins (all were 
from the same cabin) and having a program where everyone washed their 
hair with a spectal shampoo and was checked for the 'bua'. 


In addition to the above, a staff member and a C.1.T. were involved 
in a potentially serious car accident. Fortunately, it was not too 
serious with only one being kept overnight for observation. 


OOD SERVICES: 


Again this summer, | was very satisfied with the focd services of Fan 
Fare Foods. | continue to be fmpressed with our Chef Jean-Claude 
Deqlaire and the ways in which he can provide such excellent meals for 
up to 300 people. A special thanks to him also for his cooperation in 
providing special cakes, meals, etc. to fit into the programs. 


As we know, food costs have increased by 18% In the last vear. Our 
budget figure of $55,000. for ‘78 food services represented approx- 
imately a 6% increase over '77. There was the odd complaint regarding 
food quantity and variety (ie watermelon). Nevertheless, | can well 
understand the difficulties that Fan Fare had In controlling their 

own costs. 


The parents and kampors did like the food but to a lesser extent than 
in 1977. Here are the results of our post~kamp auestionnaires to 
parents rating the food: 


i974 1975 J976 AST? 1978 
Excellent 94% 8% 6% 33% 22% 
Very Good 25% 34% 17% 37% 42% 
Good 35% 37% 44% 244% 23% 
Falr 23% 194% 23% 5% 9% 
Poor 5%, 2% 10% 1% 4% 


There were occasions where some of the kitchen staff’s involvement fn 
kamp was Inappropriate. This should be discussed with Bob Gill if 

Fan Fare is with us fin '79. Also, problems with shortages of tripping 
food are a concern that should be dealt with. 


MAINTENANCE : 


Once again, Jullen Tassé and his crew had a busy summer. | shall 
always be Impressed and very grateful to Julien for his unending 
patience as he continues with the overwhelming amount of patching up, 
renovating, constructing and transplanting of buildings, water systems, 
etc. Merci Bien Julfen. 


Some of the things done this summer over and ahove the regular repairs 
and maintenance included: 


- demolition of the old ‘Longhouse’ (32' x 70!'). 

~ construction of a new storage building (14° x 16") 
and fence at the senior waterfront. 
repair of 10 rowboats. 


Malntenance Continued 


- Installing a new septic tank for the Farmhouse. 

- directing a bucket brigade (50-60 kampers and staff) 
to transport 12 tons of sand to the senior waterfront. 

- clearing of shrubbery [In junior boys section. 

- weekly pumping out of septic tanks. 

- Installing and monitoring water meters In kamp. 

~ erecting 3 flagpoles [In senior parking loft. 

- replacing mesh on backstop. 

- refinishing interior of Blockhouse and Farmhouse. 

- Installing shower and sink in the Farmhouse. 

- fitting skirts on cabooses. 

- constructing winter shelter for enlarged winter 
water reservoir. 

~ erecting a new Tee Pee across the lake. 

- weekly battles with the beavers and their dams 
at Lake Wilson. 


In terms of 1979, there are a number of things that require attention 
(non-capital in nature): 


- enlarge junior waterfront and possibly relocate. 

- replace war canoe ramp. 

- stain various parts of new recreation building - 
Katimivik 

- relocate senltor boys water pump under Katimivik. 

- stralahten out senior boys section director's 
cabin. 

- major cutting of shrubs throughout kamp. 

~ jack up kitchen water heaters. 

~ replace floor In craft shop. 

~ place another 4-6 garbage cans around kamp. 

~ replace window fixtures In Katimivik. 

- remove flreplace and small stairs at sentor 
waterfront. 

- constder wood chips on some trails to decrease 
eroslon. 

- consider a section of pavement or cement in lower 
lot for basketball.

MONTREAL OFFICE: 


It was again an extremely busy year for our kamp secrotary, Olga Hall. 
As Chairman of Public Relations for the Canadian Camping Assoctation 
and having just finished a 2 year term as President of the Quebec 
Camping Association this has required her to do much more than can 
normally be expected. | am very much grateful to her for a continued 
dedication to Kanawana and support to me. | know that the parents of 
our kampers very much appreciate her pleasant and cfficiont ways of 
dealing with them. A sincere thanks Olga! 


Also, | should not forget Helene Nollet. Although not responsible 
for kamp she has always been willing to assist us in the busy times. 
Mercl Bien Helene! 


- The non-refundable deposit required for the registration of kampers 
was increased this year. It may or may not have discouraged parents 
from cancelling a registration, however, it did decrease the loss if 
someone cancelled. This should continue or perhaps increase again 
In '79, 


- Some consideration should bo given to having 3 sessions In 1979 
rather than 4. Specifically, | am thinking of a 2 week session at 
the beginning followed by two 3 week sessions. I! know of a number 

of parents that would prefer 3 weeks to 2 and 5 weeks rather than 4. 


- Day Camp 


For the first time in many years, our kamper population of local 
children was rather significant. This trend should continue if we 
advertise in the Laurentian paper (Le Mirabel). 


It Is also worth mentioning that a number of these and other parents 
from St. Sauveur and area dropped by Kamp Kanawana and Inaufred 
about a Laurentian Day Camp. As the future of the property becomes 
clearer, a program of this sort could be considered. 


- A number of the hikes or canoe trips returned to kamp late (some~ 
times very late). Some study is required at the truck schedule vis~ 
a-vis the numbers of extended trips that are planned. In addition, 
the tripping tents of the seniors should be comprised of 4 week 
(or 5) kampers. Those only at Kamp Kanawana for 2 weeks should not 
go out on the longer (6 or 7 day) trips. 


- The new recreation hall (Katimivik) is very functional and will be 
used a great deal in the future. However, it is somewhat more 
fragile than other kamp buildings and will require some thought to 
protect it. 


-~ The staff salary ranges did not change this year. This should be 
done in 1979 particularly for counsellors where the range should be 
Increased by 25%. 


As well, there are a few auxiliary positions that could or perhaps 
should be eliminated. Some consideration should be given to this. 


Because of some of the staff problems encountered this summer, | 
feel that ‘border line’ returnee staff should not be considered. 
In previous years, we were more successful, however, as times and 
people change, it no longer seems that such a success rate with 
"border line’ returnees is likely.

CONCLUSION: 


In my stx years at Kanawana, | don't think that | have ever written a 
report that talked about problems as much as this. | look back at 
twelve weeks at kamp, working 14-18 hours a day ~ 7 days a week with 
almost seventy other staff. | leave the summer with many memories, 
some good, some not. However, | belleve that we did what we set out 
to do - Influence children in a positive way. It gives me great joy 


to know that regardless of the difficulties and problems, our kampers 
did have a very positive experience. 


In our post-kamp questionnaire, the parents were asked of their 
appraisal of Kanawana. Here Is their answer: 


1974 1975 1976 I977 1978 


ee 


Excel lent 28% 29% 30% 39.42% 39.26% 
Very Good 60 56 53 54.02 54.81 
Good iz 14 13 6.57 5.93 
Fair 0 235 4 0 0 
Poor 0 25 0 0 0 


Our successes are due to many people. To our Board of Management and 
Chairman Phil Davey, a thank you from the YMCA and Kamp Kanawana for 
their continued support, advice and indeed hard work. 


To our kampers, | shall always cherish the memories that you provide - 
it Is you that make it happen. Thanks for being a part of Kamp 
Kanawana '78. 


It is my wish that this report will be found useful not only to next 
year's Director but also to the staff of 1978. 


To the future! 
"Non Nobis Solum! 


eh Lath, 


Derek V. Walsh, 
Director of Camping.

APPRECIATION: 


As Director, | extend my thanks to- the following who contributed to 
Kamp Kanawana ‘78: 


Ivanhoe Corporation for permitting us to use the parking 
lot of the Dorval Gardens Shopping Centre as the Montreal 
terminal for kamper transportation. 


The staff of the Montreal YMCA for their continued 
encouragement and cooperation. 


Bruce Skahan for his assistance In the development of our 
astronomy program. 


Our many neighbours around kamp who so willingly permit 
us to use thelr properties and assist us in many ways. 


Canadian Paper & Packaging Company Limited for their 
donation of several rolls of paper. 


The Drug Companies who so generously donated medications 
and supplies for our infirmary. 


Gord Logan our volunteer tripper, speech writer, flying 
instructor, weatherman, advisor and counsellor - also a 
good friend. 


The Montreal Copy Centre for various free printings. 


Downtown, N.D.G. and West Island Branches of the YMCA 
for their meeting rooms. 


Eric Sandmark for the artwork on the '78 Kanawana t-shirts. 
The Clouson Company for the loan of a drink machine. 


The Town of Montreal West and Mayor Roy Locke for the loan 
of water meters this summer. 


Scotty Brotman for his kind donation of 3 books to the 
library at kamp. 


Mrs. Cairns of the Montreal Children's Library for her 
help and advice on program. 


The Energetic Company for the entertaining and educational 
skits this summer. 


Appreciation Continued 


Dr. Don Smith for his helpful visits and covering the 
infirmary at the end of the summer. 


Jack Finigan of CJAD and Dave Patrick of CFCF who spoke 
of Kanawana this summer. 


Chuck Baronowski, Director of Trails End Camp, who 
conducted the Life Saving exams. 


Roger Savard and the late Larry Chiasson of the Montreal 
Expos for the donation of 200 baseball tickets for Kanawana 
Day at the Olympic Stadium, 


Doug Myles for his assistance with our promotion of Kamp 
Kanawana and Les Voyageurs de la Verendrye.

A GLOBAL PLED( 


| pledge my loyalty to mankind: to 
speak, think, and act for the betterment 
of all peoples whatever thelr origin, 
language, or religious belief. 


To respect all properly appointed authority 
and to take only restrained and legal 
action to correct any real or imagined 
Injustice. 


To maintain the honour of the family, 
the rights, property and privacy of all 
in a free society, on principles which 
will sustain the dignity of man. 


To avoid the cause of any splritual or 
physical pollution thereby contributing 

to a cleaner, healthier, and better 

world for our children and our children's 
children; imparting to them a 

heritage of vitality, strength of 

character, and a sense of falr 

play in their dealings with their fel lowmen.
